* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Jewell County in north central Kansas...
Western Mitchell County in north central Kansas...
Eastern Osborne County in north central Kansas...
Southeastern Smith County in north central Kansas...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM CDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

that a few rounds of moderate to heavy rain since early this
morning has dumped as much as 2-5 inches across much of the area,
with the overall-highest amounts over central and southwestern
Jewell County. At least minor/nuisance flooding of various rural
roads and low-lying areas is likely to occur, and was confirmed

evening, and additional rain could fall during the day Thursday
before rain completely ends for several days. Area creeks and
rivers will also experience at least noticeable within-bank
rises, but actual flooding of main rivers is less certain.

issued Warning valid until 9 PM this evening for southern Jewell
County.

Creek, Mulberry Creek, East Twin Creek, Spring Creek, Marsh
Creek, Walnut Creek, Rock Creek, Plum Creek, Center Twin Creek,

Salt Creek, West Buffalo Creek, Dry Creek, White Rock Creek, Elm

Southeastern Harlan County in south central Nebraska...
Webster County in south central Nebraska...

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying

experience at least noticeable within- bank rises, and actual
flooding of main rivers is possible but less certain. At least
portions of the Warning area could receive at least another 1-2
inches of rain before rain eases up later tonight, and additional
rain could fall during the day Thursday before rain completely
ends for several days.

issued Flood Advisory valid until 1 AM Thursday for the same
area.
